日期：2026-03-09

115學年度「希望起飛出國交換奬學金」本院研究中心自即日起至115年4月27日(一)中午12:00止受理申請；有意願申請的同學請詳閱各項附件規定請參考傳院網站，網址如下:

[https://comm.nccu.edu.tw/PageDoc/Detail?fid=11116&id=30253](https://comm.nccu.edu.tw/PageDoc/Detail?fid=11116&id=30253)，並注意以下提交方式：

一、請於115年4月27日(一)中午12:00前將紙本文件送「達」傳播學院1樓研究中心門口信箱(Room no. 310101)，資料不齊或逾時送達，恕不收件。

二、所有紙本應備文件掃描合併成一份PDF檔案，檔名為你的名字，於115年4月27日(一)中午12:00前寄至commrd@nccu.edu.tw。

三、紙本請以雙面列印，掃描請設定200 dpi，以免檔案過大。

四、奬助名額與額度得視國合處情況及當年度經費額度調整之。

五、獲奬者須於116年7月31日前返國，並於116年9月1日前繳交相關資料以完成核銷。如無法於上述時限返國及完成核銷，請先聯繫國合處承辦人藍小姐。

六、若有相關問題，請洽承辦人電話：02-29393091分機62503 ，或電子信箱：tzushu@g.nccu.edu.tw。

七、審核結果預計於115年6月下旬公告於國合處網站。

日期：2025-08-13

本系必修課程的學生如未選課，可能影響分流評比，請本系生特別注意。

本系必修課程如下：

1.傳播概論，依課程系統顯示教室上課

2.傳播與社會，依課程系統顯示教室上課

3.傳播與當代思潮，傳院劇場上課

4.靜態影像設計(114-2學期前)，依課程系統顯示教室上課

   互動設計基礎(115-1學期起)，依課程系統顯示教室上課

5.基礎影音製作，傳院劇場上課

6.資料分析基礎與策略，傳院劇場上課

※互動設計基礎及基礎影音製作一年級上下學期都開課，上學期灌檔互動設計基礎下學期則會灌檔基礎影音製作，反之亦然。

※若有重修、補修、雙主修或輔系應修習「靜態影像設計」課程之同學，請於115-1學期起改修習「互動設計基礎」課程做為替代。

※除本系大一生灌檔必修課外，重修、補修及雙主修、輔系生請於選課期間自行選課。如需加簽請詳閱各必修課程之教學大綱。課程灌檔後請勿任意換班，以免造成無法選上必修課影響分流結果及自身權益。

※ 必修課程成績為分流評比之重要依據，恕不受理學分抵免申請。請務必依規定於修課期程內完成修習並取得及格成績，以免影響分流結果及自身權益。

日期：2022-10-03

   系所介紹

    

    「如果是在別的學校，我們就不會這樣設計！」因傳播環境變化飛快，傳統媒體市場萎縮，本院確信改革勢在必行，「改變」成為唯一的不變。因此，本院跳脫原有系所框架，並重繪傳播知識版圖，以期培養學生深度思考、多元技能，同時具備應變與創新之能力。

       本院為整合資源、鼓勵多元學習，增加學生競爭力，自2014年開始，採大一大二不分系招生與修課。之後更於2019年(108學年度)起，招收對傳播領域有興趣的自然組高中學生20名，藉此提高本院新生入學來源之多元性，同時提供不同類組學生相互交流與學習之機會。

     本系提供六門必修課(共18學分)及眾多基礎選修課，供學生選擇(詳細課程內容請見[「課程資訊」](https://umicc.nccu.edu.tw/PageDoc/Detail?fid=11063&id=18297))。此外，本系學生須於大二下，依志願及評比標準申請本院三系(新聞系、廣告系、廣播電視學系)主管學程，並自大三開始修讀，完成學位。學生畢業學位證書標註之「學系」為主管學生學程之學系，所需畢業學分等規定請見「傳播學院學生畢業修習科目表」。

 傳播學院學生所需之能力特質

        對溝通、傳播有興趣，期盼增加或擴大自己社會影響力之學生。

        喜歡思考、觀察或分析使用者行為或資訊內容之學生。

        喜歡內容或媒體設計、善於說故事，且富創意之學生。

        具文字、影音或藝術創作能力，同時具備溝通、領導能力之學生。

        善於反思，且期待突破現狀，勇於接受新挑戰之學生。

 傳播學院學生未來就業規劃

       對新聞資訊產業有興趣者，可從事如主播、記者、編輯、主持人、策展人、作家、知識型網紅、研究員等工作。

        對影音製作相關產業有興趣者，可從事如導演、編劇、製作人、成音師、攝影師、場記、美術、企畫人員等工作。

        對廣告行銷相關產業有興趣者，可從事如廣告、公關、整合行銷傳播、藝術行銷、電子商務設計等工作。

        對數位內容有興趣者，可從事遊戲設計、APP開發、數位行銷、大數據應用分析、網路編輯、網路輿情分析、提示工程師等工作。

        對公部門或非營利組織有興趣者，可從事如政府發言人、政府公關、議員、國會助理、政府觀光推廣人員，或至非營利組織工作。

[2025-08-13不分系必修課程公告本系必修課程的學生如未選課，可能影響分流評比，請本系生特別注意。

本系必修課程如下：

1.傳播概論，依課程系統顯示教室上課

2.傳播與社會，依課程系統顯示教室上課

3.傳播與當代思潮，傳院劇場上課

4.靜態影像設計(114-2學期前)，依課程系統顯示教室上課

   互動設計基礎(115-1學期起)，依課程系統顯示教室上課

5.基礎影音製作，傳院劇場上課

6.資料分析基礎與策略，傳院劇場上課

※互動設計基礎及基礎影音製作一年級上下學期都開課，上學期灌檔互動設計基礎下學期則會灌檔基礎影音製作，反之亦然。

※若有重修、補修、雙主修或輔系應修習「靜態影像設計」課程之同學，請於115-1學期起改修習「互動設計基礎」課程做為替代。

※除本系大一生灌檔必修課外，重修、補修及雙主修、輔系生請於選課期間自行選課。如需加簽請詳閱各必修課程之教學大綱。課程灌檔後請勿任意換班，以免造成無法選上必修課影響分流結果及自身權益。

Date 2022-10-04

International Admissions Information

▸International Students

International Students (Non-ROC Citizens):[NCCU International Admissions Portal (Link is external)](https://nccuadmission.nccu.edu.tw/)

 

▸Overseas Chinese, HK & Macao Students

[University Overseas Joint Admissions (Link is external)](http://www.overseas.ncnu.edu.tw)

[NCCU Independent Admissions System for Overseas Students (Link is external)](https://www.nccu.edu.tw/p/403-1000-118.php?Lang=zh-tw)

 

Academic Structure and Major Declaration

Students are all undeclared majors during their Freshman and Sophomore years to explore diverse communication fields. At the end of the Sophomore year, students will be officially streamed into the [Department of Journalism](https://jschool.nccu.edu.tw/), [Department of Advertising](https://ad.nccu.edu.tw/), or [Department of Radio-TV](https://rtv.nccu.edu.tw/PageFront). Please be advised that all majors require an internal admission review prior to official declaration. Students must meet specific departmental requirements to be admitted into their chosen program.

 

Curriculum Planning

The three departments mentioned above each offer two major professional programs, students can plan their own customized programs based on their personal aspirations and career goals.

 

Language Requirements for Students of Non-local Nationality

Most courses at our college are taught in Mandarin, with some courses supplemented by English reading materials. To ensure the quality of learning, we recommend that applicants have excellent Chinese listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills.

International applicants must pass the TOCFL (Test of Chinese as a Foreign Language) at the Learner (Level 4) or the HSK (Hanyu Shuiping Kaoshi) at Level 6, or provide equivalent proof of proficiency from other Chinese language examinations.

 

國際學生入學申請相關資訊 

▸ 國際學生 

非中華民國國籍之外籍生請點此：[政大國際生招生專區 (Link is external)](https://nccuadmission.nccu.edu.tw/)

 

▸ 僑生、港澳生 

[海外聯合招生 (Link is external)](http://www.overseas.ncnu.edu.tw)

[政大僑生與港澳生單招系統 (Link is external)](https://www.nccu.edu.tw/p/403-1000-118.php?Lang=zh-tw)

 

學制與分流說明 

本院採「大一大二不分系」制度。所有學生入學前兩年皆為未定專業 ，並於大二結束時，正式分流進入[新聞學系](https://jschool.nccu.edu.tw/) 、[廣告學系](https://ad.nccu.edu.tw/)或[廣播電視學系](https://rtv.nccu.edu.tw/PageFront) 。

重要提醒所有學生在正式確定專業前，均須先獲得該系所之錄取資格，方能完成分流程序。

課程規劃

上述三個系所分別設有兩大專業方向，學生可根據個人職涯規劃自行組織專屬課程。

非本國籍學生語言能力要求

本院多數課程以中文授課，部分課程英文閱讀材料為輔。為確保學習品質，我們建議申請者具備優異的中文聽說讀寫能力。

​國際學生申請者須通過「華語文能力測驗」高階級檢定或「新漢語水平考試」六級檢定，或具相當等級之其他華語文測驗證明。

International Leadership Courses in Communication｜Fall 2025

The College of Communication at National Chengchi University is offering the Global Communication Leadership Program in Fall 2025. This all-English taught program features five specialized courses across three key areas: media practice, cultural theory, and digital marketing.

Courses offered include:

• TV News Reporting and Live Broadcasting

• Cultural Diversity and Multilingualism in Taiwanese Media

• Computer-Mediated Communication: Theory and Practice

• Social Media and Digital Content Marketing

• Character Design and Performance for Screen

These courses are open to undergraduate students in the College of Communication (Year 1–4) and are designed for those interested in journalism, marketing, media culture, and digital communication.

Course Selection Schedule (Fall 2025 | 114-1):

Phase 1 Selection: August 19 (Mon) – August 20 (Tue)

Phase 2 Selection: August 25 (Sun) – August 27 (Tue)

Add/Drop Period: September 1 (Mon) – September 8 (Mon)

Manual Course Add (Instructor Approval Required): September 9 (Tue) – September 15 (Mon)

Course information is now available on the NCCU course selection system.

Take this opportunity to enhance both your communication expertise and English proficiency—your path to global study and career success starts here!

Date 2022-10-04

Educational Philosophy and Core Objectives

 

The College of Communication at NCCU is committed to cultivating the next generation of communication professionals. Our curriculum is thoughtfully designed to provide students with a solid foundation in communication literacy, enabling them to stand out in a rapidly changing media landscape. At the core of our program, students learn to create meaningful narratives and make these stories resonate across various platforms. Throughout their learning journey, students gain rich hands-on experience and become proficient in using a wide range of tools and technologies, including text, images, photography, sound, music, video, and web-based media. Beyond professional skills, we place great emphasis on cultivating students' humanistic values and critical thinking abilities. We encourage students to look beyond the surface, to question existing assumptions, and to deeply understand the profound social, cultural, and ethical implications of communication in contemporary society.

 

Course Structure and Module Introduction

 

All non-major students are required to take six college-wide core courses, each worth three credits. These required courses establish a comprehensive foundation for students, covering key theories, contemporary issues, and practical applications in the field of communication. In addition to this core required courses, students can freely choose from a wide range of elective courses organized into three thematic modules. 

Program Basics Module & Humanity Module guides students in exploring the cultural, philosophical, and ethical dimensions behind media and communication. 

 

The Program Capacity Module provides foundational knowledge in professional fields such as journalism, advertising, and broadcasting. 

 

The Integrated Module encourages interdisciplinary learning and real-world problem-solving through courses in data analysis and programming fundamentals. This modular curriculum structure allows students to tailor their personalized learning journey based on their unique interests, passions, and career goals, thereby gaining a truly comprehensive and transformative educational experience.

[:::](http:umicc.nccu.edu.tw/PageDoc/Detail?fid=11077&id=18178#accesskey-c)

Date 2022-10-04

 

Introduction to the Undeclared Major in College of Communication

In an era defined by a rapidly evolving media landscape, we operate under the core philosophy that “change” is the only unchangeable constant. Moving beyond the traditional boundaries of communication disciplines, the NCCU College of Communication has reconstructed its knowledge framework to integrate critical thinking with creative execution. Our curriculum is specifically designed to equip students not only with fundamental communication skills but also with the innovative capacity required to navigate and shape the future of global media.

To consolidate our resources and foster a truly interdisciplinary learning environment, the College has implemented an "Undeclared Major" system for all first and second year undergraduates since 2014. This structure encourages students to explore diverse communication fields before specializing, thereby enhancing their overall competitiveness. In a further commitment to diversity, we began admitting twenty students from the natural sciences track in 2019. By integrating students from both social and natural science backgrounds, we create a dynamic platform for cross-disciplinary exchange that enriches academic experience for the entire community.

Our curriculum provides a robust foundation through six compulsory core courses (18 credits) and a diverse selection of electives. During the second semester of their sophomore year, students apply to one of our three specialized departments. Journalism, Advertising, or Radio & Television based on their personal aspirations and academic performance. Specialized departmental study officially commences in junior year. Upon completion of the program, the student's primary department will be formally recognized on their diploma. For a comprehensive guide to graduation requirements and credit structures, please refer to the [Diploma Requirements](https://umicc.nccu.edu.tw/PageDoc/Detail?fid=11063&id=18297).

Student Profiles and Core Competencies

We welcome students who possess a profound interest in communication and a strong aspiration to expand their social impact. Our ideal candidates are those who find fulfillment in critical thinking, whether through observing user behavior or analyzing media content. We seek creative individuals who excel at storytelling and media design, as well as those with proven talents in writing, filmmaking, or the arts, complemented by strong communication and leadership skills. Above all, we value reflective practitioners who are committed to challenging the status quo and are prepared to embrace new challenges with enthusiasm.

Career Trajectories and Professional Development

Graduates of our College are equipped to pursue diverse professional paths across several core industries. Graduates who are interested in the News media and Information industry can consider the following career options such as Anchor, Journalist, Editor, TV or Radio Show Host, Information Curator, Writer, Social Media Influencer, and Researcher. 

For students passionate about Video Production, opportunities abound in roles such as Director, Script Writer, Producer, Script Supervisor, Director of Photography, and Event Planner. 

Furthermore, those interested in Marketing and Advertising are prepared for excellence in public relations, integrated marketing communications, art marketing, and e-commerce design.

As the digital landscape evolves, students focused on Digital Content can venture into game design, app development, and digital marketing, or specialize in emerging fields such as big data analysis, web editing, internet sentiment analysis, and prompt engineering.

Beyond the private sector, our program also prepares graduates for impactful roles within public and voluntary sectors. Graduates who are interested in public service can consider the following career options such as Spokesperson, Politician, Government PR, Legislative Assistant, and Government Tourism Promoter.

日期：2025-08-13

本系必修課程的學生如未選課，可能影響分流評比，請本系生特別注意。

本系必修課程如下：

1.傳播概論

2.傳播與社會

3.傳播與當代思潮

4.靜態影像設計(114學年第二學期前) 互動設計基礎 (115學期起)

5.基礎影音製作

6.資料分析基礎與策略

※互動設計基礎及基礎影音製作一年級上下學期都開課，上學期灌檔互動設計基礎下學期則會灌檔基礎影音製作，反之亦然。

※若有重修、補修、雙主修或輔系應修習「靜態影像設計」課程之同學，請於115-1學期起改修習「互動設計基礎」課程做為替代。

※除本系大一生灌檔必修課外，重修、補修及雙主修、輔系生請於選課期間自行選課。如需加簽請詳閱各必修課程之教學大綱。課程灌檔後請勿任意換班，以免造成無法選上必修課影響分流結果及自身權益。

※ 必修課程成績為分流評比之重要依據，恕不受理學分抵免申請。請務必依規定於修課期程內完成修習並取得及格成績，以免影響分流結果及自身權益。

   系所介紹

    

    「如果是在別的學校，我們就不會這樣設計！」因傳播環境變化飛快，傳統媒體市場萎縮，本院確信改革勢在必行，「改變」成為唯一的不變。因此，本院跳脫原有系所框架，並重繪傳播知識版圖，以期培養學生深度思考、多元技能，同時具備應變與創新之能力。

       本院為整合資源、鼓勵多元學習，增加學生競爭力，自2014年開始，採大一大二不分系招生與修課。之後更於2019年(108學年度)起，招收對傳播領域有興趣的自然組高中學生20名，藉此提高本院新生入學來源之多元性，同時提供不同類組學生相互交流與學習之機會。

     本系提供六門必修課(共18學分)及眾多基礎選修課，供學生選擇(詳細課程內容請見[「課程資訊」](https://umicc.nccu.edu.tw/PageDoc/Detail?fid=11063&id=18297))。此外，本系學生須於大二下，依志願及評比標準申請本院三系(新聞系、廣告系、廣播電視學系)主管學程，並自大三開始修讀，完成學位。學生畢業學位證書標註之「學系」為主管學生學程之學系，所需畢業學分等規定請見「傳播學院學生畢業修習科目表」。

 傳播學院學生所需之能力特質

        對溝通、傳播有興趣，期盼增加或擴大自己社會影響力之學生。

        喜歡思考、觀察或分析使用者行為或資訊內容之學生。

        喜歡內容或媒體設計、善於說故事，且富創意之學生。

        具文字、影音或藝術創作能力，同時具備溝通、領導能力之學生。

        善於反思，且期待突破現狀，勇於接受新挑戰之學生。

 傳播學院學生未來就業規劃

       對新聞資訊產業有興趣者，可從事如主播、記者、編輯、主持人、策展人、作家、知識型網紅、研究員等工作。

        對影音製作相關產業有興趣者，可從事如導演、編劇、製作人、成音師、攝影師、場記、美術、企畫人員等工作。

        對廣告行銷相關產業有興趣者，可從事如廣告、公關、整合行銷傳播、藝術行銷、電子商務設計等工作。

        對數位內容有興趣者，可從事遊戲設計、APP開發、數位行銷、大數據應用分析、網路編輯、網路輿情分析、提示工程師等工作。

        對公部門或非營利組織有興趣者，可從事如政府發言人、政府公關、議員、國會助理、政府觀光推廣人員，或至非營利組織工作。

Date 2022-10-04

International Admissions Information

▸International Students

International Students (Non-ROC Citizens):[NCCU International Admissions Portal (Link is external)](https://nccuadmission.nccu.edu.tw/)

 

▸Overseas Chinese, HK & Macao Students

[University Overseas Joint Admissions (Link is external)](http://www.overseas.ncnu.edu.tw)

[NCCU Independent Admissions System for Overseas Students (Link is external)](https://www.nccu.edu.tw/p/403-1000-118.php?Lang=zh-tw)

 

Academic Structure and Major Declaration

Students are all undeclared majors during their Freshman and Sophomore years to explore diverse communication fields. At the end of the Sophomore year, students will be officially streamed into the [Department of Journalism](https://jschool.nccu.edu.tw/), [Department of Advertising](https://ad.nccu.edu.tw/), or [Department of Radio-TV](https://rtv.nccu.edu.tw/PageFront). Please be advised that all majors require an internal admission review prior to official declaration. Students must meet specific departmental requirements to be admitted into their chosen program.

 

Curriculum Planning

The three departments mentioned above each offer two major professional programs, students can plan their own customized programs based on their personal aspirations and career goals.

 

Language Requirements for Students of Non-local Nationality

Most courses at our college are taught in Mandarin, with some courses supplemented by English reading materials. To ensure the quality of learning, we recommend that applicants have excellent Chinese listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills.

International applicants must pass the TOCFL (Test of Chinese as a Foreign Language) at the Learner (Level 4) or the HSK (Hanyu Shuiping Kaoshi) at Level 6, or provide equivalent proof of proficiency from other Chinese language examinations.

 

國際學生入學申請相關資訊 

▸ 國際學生 

非中華民國國籍之外籍生請點此：[政大國際生招生專區 (Link is external)](https://nccuadmission.nccu.edu.tw/)

 

▸ 僑生、港澳生 

[海外聯合招生 (Link is external)](http://www.overseas.ncnu.edu.tw)

[政大僑生與港澳生單招系統 (Link is external)](https://www.nccu.edu.tw/p/403-1000-118.php?Lang=zh-tw)

 

學制與分流說明 

本院採「大一大二不分系」制度。所有學生入學前兩年皆為未定專業 ，並於大二結束時，正式分流進入[新聞學系](https://jschool.nccu.edu.tw/) 、[廣告學系](https://ad.nccu.edu.tw/)或[廣播電視學系](https://rtv.nccu.edu.tw/PageFront) 。

重要提醒所有學生在正式確定專業前，均須先獲得該系所之錄取資格，方能完成分流程序。

課程規劃

上述三個系所分別設有兩大專業方向，學生可根據個人職涯規劃自行組織專屬課程。

非本國籍學生語言能力要求

本院多數課程以中文授課，部分課程英文閱讀材料為輔。為確保學習品質，我們建議申請者具備優異的中文聽說讀寫能力。

​國際學生申請者須通過「華語文能力測驗」高階級檢定或「新漢語水平考試」六級檢定，或具相當等級之其他華語文測驗證明。

Date 2022-10-04

Educational Philosophy and Core Objectives

 

The College of Communication at NCCU is committed to cultivating the next generation of communication professionals. Our curriculum is thoughtfully designed to provide students with a solid foundation in communication literacy, enabling them to stand out in a rapidly changing media landscape. At the core of our program, students learn to create meaningful narratives and make these stories resonate across various platforms. Throughout their learning journey, students gain rich hands-on experience and become proficient in using a wide range of tools and technologies, including text, images, photography, sound, music, video, and web-based media. Beyond professional skills, we place great emphasis on cultivating students' humanistic values and critical thinking abilities. We encourage students to look beyond the surface, to question existing assumptions, and to deeply understand the profound social, cultural, and ethical implications of communication in contemporary society.

 

Course Structure and Module Introduction

 

All non-major students are required to take six college-wide core courses, each worth three credits. These required courses establish a comprehensive foundation for students, covering key theories, contemporary issues, and practical applications in the field of communication. In addition to this core required courses, students can freely choose from a wide range of elective courses organized into three thematic modules. 

Program Basics Module & Humanity Module guides students in exploring the cultural, philosophical, and ethical dimensions behind media and communication. 

 

The Program Capacity Module provides foundational knowledge in professional fields such as journalism, advertising, and broadcasting. 

 

The Integrated Module encourages interdisciplinary learning and real-world problem-solving through courses in data analysis and programming fundamentals. This modular curriculum structure allows students to tailor their personalized learning journey based on their unique interests, passions, and career goals, thereby gaining a truly comprehensive and transformative educational experience.

International Leadership Courses in Communication｜Fall 2025

The College of Communication at National Chengchi University is offering the Global Communication Leadership Program in Fall 2025. This all-English taught program features five specialized courses across three key areas: media practice, cultural theory, and digital marketing.

Courses offered include:

• TV News Reporting and Live Broadcasting

• Cultural Diversity and Multilingualism in Taiwanese Media

• Computer-Mediated Communication: Theory and Practice

• Social Media and Digital Content Marketing

• Character Design and Performance for Screen

These courses are open to undergraduate students in the College of Communication (Year 1–4) and are designed for those interested in journalism, marketing, media culture, and digital communication.

Course Selection Schedule (Fall 2025 | 114-1):

Phase 1 Selection: August 19 (Mon) – August 20 (Tue)

Phase 2 Selection: August 25 (Sun) – August 27 (Tue)

Add/Drop Period: September 1 (Mon) – September 8 (Mon)

Manual Course Add (Instructor Approval Required): September 9 (Tue) – September 15 (Mon)

Course information is now available on the NCCU course selection system.

Take this opportunity to enhance both your communication expertise and English proficiency—your path to global study and career success starts here!

text:

[:::](http:umicc.nccu.edu.tw/PageDoc/Detail?fid=11077&id=18178#accesskey-c)

Date 2022-10-04

 

Introduction to the Undeclared Major in College of Communication

In an era defined by a rapidly evolving media landscape, we operate under the core philosophy that “change” is the only unchangeable constant. Moving beyond the traditional boundaries of communication disciplines, the NCCU College of Communication has reconstructed its knowledge framework to integrate critical thinking with creative execution. Our curriculum is specifically designed to equip students not only with fundamental communication skills but also with the innovative capacity required to navigate and shape the future of global media.

To consolidate our resources and foster a truly interdisciplinary learning environment, the College has implemented an "Undeclared Major" system for all first and second year undergraduates since 2014. This structure encourages students to explore diverse communication fields before specializing, thereby enhancing their overall competitiveness. In a further commitment to diversity, we began admitting twenty students from the natural sciences track in 2019. By integrating students from both social and natural science backgrounds, we create a dynamic platform for cross-disciplinary exchange that enriches academic experience for the entire community.

Our curriculum provides a robust foundation through six compulsory core courses (18 credits) and a diverse selection of electives. During the second semester of their sophomore year, students apply to one of our three specialized departments. Journalism, Advertising, or Radio & Television based on their personal aspirations and academic performance. Specialized departmental study officially commences in junior year. Upon completion of the program, the student's primary department will be formally recognized on their diploma. For a comprehensive guide to graduation requirements and credit structures, please refer to the [Diploma Requirements](https://umicc.nccu.edu.tw/PageDoc/Detail?fid=11063&id=18297).

Student Profiles and Core Competencies

We welcome students who possess a profound interest in communication and a strong aspiration to expand their social impact. Our ideal candidates are those who find fulfillment in critical thinking, whether through observing user behavior or analyzing media content. We seek creative individuals who excel at storytelling and media design, as well as those with proven talents in writing, filmmaking, or the arts, complemented by strong communication and leadership skills. Above all, we value reflective practitioners who are committed to challenging the status quo and are prepared to embrace new challenges with enthusiasm.

Career Trajectories and Professional Development

Graduates of our College are equipped to pursue diverse professional paths across several core industries. Graduates who are interested in the News media and Information industry can consider the following career options such as Anchor, Journalist, Editor, TV or Radio Show Host, Information Curator, Writer, Social Media Influencer, and Researcher. 

For students passionate about Video Production, opportunities abound in roles such as Director, Script Writer, Producer, Script Supervisor, Director of Photography, and Event Planner. 

Furthermore, those interested in Marketing and Advertising are prepared for excellence in public relations, integrated marketing communications, art marketing, and e-commerce design.

As the digital landscape evolves, students focused on Digital Content can venture into game design, app development, and digital marketing, or specialize in emerging fields such as big data analysis, web editing, internet sentiment analysis, and prompt engineering.

Beyond the private sector, our program also prepares graduates for impactful roles within public and voluntary sectors. Graduates who are interested in public service can consider the following career options such as Spokesperson, Politician, Government PR, Legislative Assistant, and Government Tourism Promoter.
